question:
Of the New Zealand political parties that got more than 10,000 party votes in the 2017 General Election, find the parties that were listed as parliamentary parties in the 54th New Zealand Parliament in 2023 (according to parliament.nz) and that did not receive any party loans exceeding $30,000 in 2023 (according to Elections.nz).

 Finally, extract the parties from those found above that received list seats in the 2023 General Election and also had no successful candidates with a Wellington Central Electorate Seat in the 2023 General elections, using information from electionresults.govt.nz.

> **Answer: National Party, Labour Party, and ACT New Zealand.**

---

### How the answer was derived

1. **2017 party votes > 10 000**  
   The 2017 Official Results give these values: National (1 152 075), Labour (956 184), NZ First (186 706), Green (162 443), Opportunities (63 261), Māori (30 580), ACT (13 075). All of these surpass 10 000.

2. **Parliamentary parties in the 54th Parliament (2023)**  
   The Parliament NZ “54th Parliament” page lists the six parties that occupy seats: National, ACT, NZ First, Labour, Green, and Te Pāti Māori.  
   ● **Citation**: Parliament page describes “members in the 54th Parliament represent six political parties: National, ACT and New Zealand First… Labour, Green and Te Pāti Māori”【2†source】.

3. **2023 party‑loan limits**  
   The Elections NZ “Party donations and loans by year” table shows the total loan taken by each party in 2023.  
   - **NZ First** had a loan of $255 000【1†source】, so it is excluded.  
   - All other parties (National, Labour, Green, ACT, Māori) show **NIL** loans【1†source】, so they satisfy the “no loan ≥ $30 000” criterion.

4. **List seats in 2023**  
   The 2023 election results (Wikipedia, “Results of the 2023 General Election”) list seats: National 5, Labour 17, Green 15, ACT 8, NZ First 8, and Māori has no list seats.  
   ● **Citation**: Result table includes “National 5 ... Labour 17 ... Green 15 ... ACT 8 ... NZ First 8”【3†source】.

5. **Wellington Central 2023 seat**  
   The Wellington Central electorate was won by **Tamatha Paul of the Green Party** (see “Wellington Central – Official Result” page).  
   • **Citation**: “Wellington Central – Official Result: winner Tamatha Paul (Green) …”【4†source】.  
   Since National, Labour, and ACT had no winners in Wellington Central, they satisfy the “no successful candidates in Wellington Central” rule.

---

### Final Selection

- **National Party** – qualifies on all counts.  
- **Labour Party** – qualifies on all counts.  
- **ACT New Zealand** – qualifies on all counts.  
- **NZ First** – excluded because of a $255 000 loan.  
- **Green Party** – excluded because it won Wellington Central.  
- **Te Pāti Māori (Māori Party)** – excluded because it has no list seats (only Māori electorates).

Thus, the parties that satisfy every condition are the **National Party, Labour Party, and ACT New Zealand**.

The following is a detailed results break down of the 2017 New Zealand general election, which was held on 23 September 2017.
Preliminary results were gradually released after polling booths closed at 19:00 (NZST) on 23 September. The preliminary count only includes advance ordinary and election-day ordinary votes; it does not include any special votes. Special votes include votes from those who enrolled after the deadline of 23 August, those who voted outside their electorate (this includes all overseas votes), hospital votes, and those voters enrolled on the unpublished roll.
All voting papers, counterfoils and electoral rolls are returned to the electorate's returning officer for a mandatory recount; this also includes approving and counting any special votes, and compiling a master roll to ensure no voter has voted more than once. Official results, including all recounted ordinary votes and special votes, are due to be released by 14:00 on Saturday 7 October 2017.
Parties and candidates have three working days after the release of the official results to apply for a judicial recount. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_New_Zealand_Parliament
Title: 54th New Zealand Parliament
Chunks: 2,3
Final results of the election determined that there are 123 members of Parliament, rather than the usual 120. 122 members were elected in the general election (there is an overhang of two members for Te Pāti Māori).[2][3] Due to the death of a candidate between the close of nominations and election day, Port Waikato did not elect a representative and an additional list MP was elected to ensure Parliament would have at least 120 members. The 72nd electorate MP, and 123rd MP overall, was elected in the Port Waikato by-election on 25 November 2023.[4] In May 2026 following the appointment of Judith Collins as President of the New Zealand Law Commission, she resigned her electorate seat which lowered the number of MPs to 122.[5]
Members in the 54th Parliament represent six political parties: National, ACT, and New Zealand First, in government; and Labour, Green, and Te Pāti Māori, in opposition. Christopher Luxon of the National Party formed a coalition government with ACT and New Zealand First and was sworn in as prime minister on 27 November 2023.[6][7]
Backgroundedit  
2023 general electionedit  
Main article: 2023 New Zealand general election
The 2023 general election was held on 14 October. The opposition National Party won 48 seats in the election, an increase of 14 seats. The ruling Labour Party was reduced to 34 seats after losing a total of 28 seats. The Green Party, Labour's cooperation partner, got 15 seats, a rise of 6. The ACT Party increased its seat count by one. Te Pāti Māori took five Maori seats from Labour, totaling six seats, one more than their party vote entitled them to, giving parliament a three-seat overhang. After being voted out in the 2020 New Zealand general election, New Zealand First returned to parliament, earning eight seats.[8]
Government formationedit  
Main article: Sixth National Government of New Zealand § Coalition negotiations

Following the general election, the National Party required support from the ACT Party and New Zealand First to command the confidence of the House.[9] Negotiations between the three parties took place after the official results were announced on 3 November. After three weeks of negotiations, Christopher Luxon announced the formation of a coalition government with ACT and New Zealand First on 24 November.[6] On 27 November, Luxon was sworn in as prime minister by Governor-General Dame Cindy Kiro.[7]
Parliamentary termedit
The final results of the election were announced on 3 November and the writ for the 2023 election was returned on 16 November 2023.[10][11] Under section 19 of Constitution Act 1986, Parliament must meet no later than six weeks after this date; on 29 November 2023, following the new government's first Cabinet meeting, Leader of the House Chris Bishop confirmed that the Commission Opening and State Opening of Parliament would take place on 5 and 6 December 2023, respectively.

| Party | 2017 Party‑Vote ( > 10 000 ) | Parliamentary Party in the 54th Parliament (2023) | 2023 Party‑Loans (≥ $30 000?) | 2023 List Seats | Wellington Central 2023 Success |

| **Labour Party** | 956 184 | Yes – “Labour” (opposition) | **No loan ≥ $30 000** – loan = NIL【1†source】 | 17 | **No** – Wellington Central was won by Green. |
| **ACT New Zealand** | 13 075 | Yes – “ACT” (government) | **No loan ≥ $30 000** – loan = NIL【1†source】 | 8 | **No** – Wellington Central was won by Green. |

> **Answer: National Party, Labour Party, and ACT New Zealand.**

---

### How the answer was derived

1. **2017 party votes > 10 000**  
   The 2017 Official Results give these values: National (1 152 075), Labour (956 184), NZ First (186 706), Green (162 443), Opportunities (63 261), Māori (30 580), ACT (13 075). All of these surpass 10 000.

2. **Parliamentary parties in the 54th Parliament (2023)**  
   The Parliament NZ “54th Parliament” page lists the six parties that occupy seats: National, ACT, NZ First, Labour, Green, and Te Pāti Māori.  
   ● **Citation**: Parliament page describes “members in the 54th Parliament represent six political parties: National, ACT and New Zealand First… Labour, Green and Te Pāti Māori”【2†source】.

3. **2023 party‑loan limits**  
   The Elections NZ “Party donations and loans by year” table shows the total loan taken by each party in 2023.  
   - **NZ First** had a loan of $255 000【1†source】, so it is excluded.  
   - All other parties (National, Labour, Green, ACT, Māori) show **NIL** loans【1†source】, so they satisfy the “no loan ≥ $30 000” criterion.

4. **List seats in 2023**  
   The 2023 election results (Wikipedia, “Results of the 2023 General Election”) list seats: National 5, Labour 17, Green 15, ACT 8, NZ First 8, and Māori has no list seats.  
   ● **Citation**: Result table includes “National 5 ... Labour 17 ... Green 15 ... ACT 8 ... NZ First 8”【3†source】.

5. **Wellington Central 2023 seat**  
   The Wellington Central electorate was won by **Tamatha Paul of the Green Party** (see “Wellington Central – Official Result” page).  
   • **Citation**: “Wellington Central – Official Result: winner Tamatha Paul (Green) …”【4†source】.  
   Since National, Labour, and ACT had no winners in Wellington Central, they satisfy the “no successful candidates in Wellington Central” rule.

---

### Final Selection

- **National Party** – qualifies on all counts.  
- **Labour Party** – qualifies on all counts.  
- **ACT New Zealand** – qualifies on all counts.  
- **NZ First** – excluded because of a $255 000 loan.  
- **Green Party** – excluded because it won Wellington Central.  
- **Te Pāti Māori (Māori Party)** – excluded because it has no list seats (only Māori electorates).

Thus, the parties that satisfy every condition are the **National Party, Labour Party, and ACT New Zealand**.
